## MCP server

Expose nbskill notebook operations as native MCP tools. This is the
preferred integration for careful single-notebook reads and edits
because multiline notebook cells travel as structured tool arguments
rather than shell-quoted strings.

The server now favors verifiable context: batch edits include read-back
hashes, symbol graph calls include complete structured usage data, and
generated-file warnings are reserved for changes that touch exported
notebook code.

The command-line functions are useful on their own, but coding agents
work best when the same operations are available as structured tools.
This notebook exposes the project through a FastMCP server while keeping
the server layer thin and predictable.

### Production contract

The MCP server exposes the production core through stable structured
tools. Tool schemas exclude uncommon Python-only operations, responses
include concise text plus structured content, diagnostics are scoped to
touched notebooks when possible, edit tools report feedback without raw
notebook JSON, and experimental tools are omitted from default
production use.

The MCP server should stay boring on purpose. Each tool accepts
structured arguments, captures printed output, uses notebook locks where
file operations can collide, and delegates the actual work to the same
functions tested elsewhere.

``` python
def demo_tool():
    print("captured output")
```

#### A small MCP result

The first example uses the imported public surface so readers can see
the text returned by
[`capture_call`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/mcp.html#capture_call)
and the server type without starting a transport.

### File-based reload imports

FastMCP 3 reload executes the selected file as an un-packaged module.
`nbskill.mcp` therefore declares its package when needed before its
relative imports run; regular package imports already have the correct
package and are unchanged.

### Capturing command output

The MCP tools should return text, not leak stdout and stderr into the
server process. These helpers capture each underlying function call and
convert its visible result into one response string.

#### Text and output normalization

[`as_text`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/mcp.html#as_text)
keeps every tool wrapper on one response contract. It turns an absent
result into empty output while leaving ordinary values readable.

### Isolated notebook operations

[`edit_notebook_tool`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/mcp.html#edit_notebook_tool)
and
[`exec_nb_tool`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/mcp.html#exec_nb_tool)
run notebook mutation and execution in importable multiprocessing
workers instead of doing the work directly in MCP worker threads. This
is intentional. If an MCP client times out, cancelling an
`asyncio.to_thread` wait does not stop the underlying Python thread; the
old work can keep exporting notebooks and consuming memory after the
client has already given up.

A process gives the server a boundary it can terminate. The worker
target is a normal module function, not a string passed to `python -c`,
so the code is readable, importable under spawn, and covered by notebook
tests. On POSIX the worker starts a process group with `setsid`, which
lets timeout cleanup terminate nested export work too.

Each child owns the notebook locks for its actual transaction. The
parent must not retain a process-scoped notebook lock while waiting for
that child: the worker would block on the parent and both sides would
wait until timeout.
[`edit_notebook_tool`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/mcp.html#edit_notebook_tool)
caps `tool_timeout` at 110 seconds so it can return a structured timeout
before clients with a 120 second transport deadline give up.

## Diagnostics and log reports

The server records enough information to diagnose failures after a
client disconnects. Log parsing stays separate from transport middleware
so reports can be tested with small JSONL fixtures.

MCP postmortems need every tool call to leave enough evidence to answer
three questions later: did it finish, how long did it take, and how much
output did it produce. The middleware logs these fields at the server
boundary so individual tools do not each need bespoke timing code.

The log reporter intentionally accepts older log files. Older rows do
not have call ids or output lengths, so the report pairs what it can and
calls out missing evidence as a problem instead of pretending the
history is cleaner than it is.

#### Report a log window

[`mcp_log_report`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/mcp.html#mcp_log_report)
pairs start and end events, then groups incomplete or malformed records
into actionable problems. A missing path is a useful small example
because it exercises the same report shape without needing a running
server.

### Compact MCP results

Normal calls place one human summary in visible MCP text and place each
structured fact once. `detail="debug"` adds raw diagnostics and
arguments for troubleshooting. Failures state the type, cause, and next
action without returning a Python traceback.

``` python

debug = mcp_tool_result("demo", {}, "stored only in debug", detail="debug")
print(normal.content[0].text)
print(debug.structured_content["debug"]["raw_output"])
```

### Registering notebook tools

The wrapper should preserve useful structure, not flatten everything
into text.
[`context`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/read.html#context)
uses `overview` for compact versus focused detail, and project-level
calls can attach the notebook knowledge graph with `include_graph=True`.
Cell or symbol targets include symbol graph payloads so MCP clients can
inspect impact without parsing prose.

Edit and execution wrappers also adapt to MCP-specific transport.
[`update_cell`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/write.html#update_cell)
accepts `new_lines` so exact source can be sent directly without
temporary files, and unsafe
[`exec_nb`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/execute.html#exec_nb)
runs in an isolated process so the MCP server can terminate runaway
execution without blocking worker threads.

### Small MCP surface

The public MCP server exposes nine tools for the normal notebook
workflow:
[`context`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/read.html#context),
[`edit_notebook`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/edit.html#edit_notebook),
[`exec_nb`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/execute.html#exec_nb),
`verify_change`, `doctor`,
[`diff_nb`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/review.html#diff_nb),
[`create_notebook`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/write.html#create_notebook),
`reference`, and `healthcheck`.

[`context`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/read.html#context)
is the only read surface: start with `view="summary"`, then narrow by
`chapter`, `cell_type`, `query`, `include_re`, `exclude_re`, or
`context_lines`. Use `doctor(scopes="style")` for style diagnostics;
there is no separate style tool.

[`edit_notebook`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/edit.html#edit_notebook)
supports
[`replace_cell`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/foundation.html#replace_cell),
`insert_cells`, `delete_cells`,
[`move_cells`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/write.html#move_cells),
`explode_cells`,
[`replace_lines`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/edit.html#replace_lines),
[`insert_lines`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/edit.html#insert_lines),
[`delete_lines`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/edit.html#delete_lines),
[`replace_text`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/edit.html#replace_text),
and
[`replace_texts`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/edit.html#replace_texts).
Existing cells use `cell_id`, `cell_ids`, or `target="all"`; whole-cell
payloads use `source` or `source_lines`, structural edits use `cells`
plus `anchor_id`/`where`, and text edits are literal. Add
`expected_hash` when stale context must fail, and use `dry_run=True` to
preview.

[`exec_nb_tool`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/mcp.html#exec_nb_tool)
always uses safe execution and accepts no caller-supplied bypasses. If a
new cell is blocked, nbskill asks the connected MCP client to approve
its exact source hash, then makes one internal retry. A client without
approval prompts receives a refusal.

### Verify explicitly affected notebooks

`verify_change` accepts only named notebooks. It reviews each diff, runs
a safe in-memory check through the last changed code cell unless an
`up2id` override is supplied, and scopes `doctor` to that notebook. The
reports stay separate so one failure does not hide the results for the
others.

FastMCP reload are separate so notebook examples can inspect the public
surface without opening a long-running transport.

### MCP transport-friendly edits

MCP clients send exact source directly. `source_lines` avoids
JSON-string plans and temporary files, which is useful when the source
being written contains escaped notebook text. Unsafe notebook execution
remains isolated so timeouts can terminate runaway work.

``` python
mcp_tools = {tool.name: tool for tool in await mcp.list_tools()}
assert not {"convert", "problem_memory", "visible_text_inventory"} & set(mcp_tools)
edit_parameters = str(mcp_tools["edit_notebook"].parameters)
assert "edits" in edit_parameters and "dry_run" in edit_parameters
assert "feedback" not in edit_parameters and "default_cell_type" not in edit_parameters
context_parameters = str(mcp_tools["context"].parameters)
assert all(name in context_parameters for name in ("target", "scope", "view", "chapter", "cell_type", "query", "include_re", "exclude_re", "context_lines", "max_matches", "max_chars_per_cell", "include_output", "line_numbers", "include_graph"))
assert not any(name in context_parameters for name in ("targets", "mode", "around"))
assert "filter_context" not in mcp_tools
reference_parameters = str(mcp_tools["reference"].parameters)
assert "query" in reference_parameters and "top_k" in reference_parameters and "action" not in reference_parameters
doctor_parameters = str(mcp_tools["doctor"].parameters)
assert "scopes" in doctor_parameters and "detail" not in doctor_parameters and "fix" not in doctor_parameters
assert "style_check" not in mcp_tools
diff_parameters = str(mcp_tools["diff_nb"].parameters)
assert "max_output_chars" in diff_parameters
assert "edit_cell" not in mcp_tools
print("direct MCP schema exposes one context reader and doctor-owned diagnostics")
```

``` python
with write_demo_notebook("07_mcp_insert_cells.ipynb") as edit_nb:
    edit_nb = edit_nb.resolve()
    nb = new_nb([mk_cell('payload = "old"')])
    anchor_id = nb.cells[0].id
    _write_raw_nb(nb, edit_nb)
    result = await mcp.call_tool("edit_notebook", {"path": str(edit_nb), "edits": [dict(op="insert_cells", anchor_id=anchor_id, cells=[dict(source_lines=["inserted = True"])])]})
    assert result.structured_content["changed"] is True
    assert _read_raw_nb(edit_nb).cells[1].source == "inserted = True"
    print("direct MCP edit_notebook inserts structured cells")
```

``` python
with write_demo_notebook("07_mcp_edit_notebook.ipynb") as edit_nb:
    edit_nb = edit_nb.resolve()
    nb = new_nb([mk_cell('payload = "old"\nother = 1')])
    edit_cell_id = nb.cells[0].id
    _write_raw_nb(nb, edit_nb)
    exact_source = 'payload = "line 1' + chr(92) + 'nline 2"'
    edit_result = await mcp.call_tool("edit_notebook", {"path": str(edit_nb), "edits": [dict(op="replace_cell", cell_id=edit_cell_id, source_lines=[exact_source])]})
    assert edit_result.structured_content["changed"] is True
    assert _read_raw_nb(edit_nb).cells[0].source == exact_source
    range_result = await mcp.call_tool("edit_notebook", {"path": str(edit_nb), "edits": [dict(op="replace_lines", cell_id=edit_cell_id, start_line=1, end_line=1, replacement_lines=['payload = "range"'])]})
    assert range_result.structured_content["changed"] is True
    assert _read_raw_nb(edit_nb).cells[0].source == 'payload = "range"'
    feedback_result = await mcp.call_tool("edit_notebook", {"path": str(edit_nb), "edits": [dict(op="replace_cell", cell_id=edit_cell_id, source_lines=["print('mcp feedback')"])]})
    assert feedback_result.structured_content["changed"] is True
    assert _read_raw_nb(edit_nb).cells[0].outputs == []
    print("direct MCP edit_notebook preserves escaped newlines")
```

``` python
out = StringIO()
with _demo_root("07_mcp_context_graph") as graph_root:
    lib_nb = graph_root / "lib.ipynb"
    call_nb = graph_root / "call.ipynb"
    _write_raw_nb(new_nb([mk_cell("#| export\ndef thing():\n    return 1")]), lib_nb)
    _write_raw_nb(new_nb([mk_cell("from nbskill.lib import thing\nvalue = thing()")]), call_nb)
    context_args = dict(target="thing", scope=str(graph_root))
    with redirect_stdout(out): context_result = await mcp.call_tool("context", context_args)
    graph_payload = context_result.structured_content["context"]["symbol_graphs"][0]
    assert graph_payload["caller_usages"][0]["line"] == "value = thing()"
    assert out.getvalue() == ""
    print("structured context symbol usages:", len(graph_payload["caller_usages"]))
```

``` python
    dry_result = await mcp.call_tool("edit_notebook", {"path": str(edit_nb), "edits": [dict(op="replace_cell", cell_id=cell_id, source_lines=[exact_source])], "dry_run": True})
    assert dry_result.structured_content["changed"] is True
    assert dry_result.structured_content["dry_run"] is True
    assert dry_result.structured_content["affected_cell_ids"] == [cell_id]
    assert dry_result.structured_content["before_hash"] == dry_result.structured_content["after_hash"]
    assert dry_result.structured_content["planned_hash"] != dry_result.structured_content["before_hash"]
    assert _read_raw_nb(edit_nb).cells[0].source == 'payload = "old"\nvalue = 1'

    edit_result = await mcp.call_tool("edit_notebook", {"path": str(edit_nb), "edits": [dict(op="replace_cell", cell_id=cell_id, source_lines=[exact_source])]})
    assert edit_result.structured_content["changed"] is True
    assert _read_raw_nb(edit_nb).cells[0].source == exact_source

    range_result = await mcp.call_tool("edit_notebook", {"path": str(edit_nb), "edits": [dict(op="replace_lines", cell_id=cell_id, start_line=1, end_line=1, replacement_lines=['payload = "range"'])]})
    assert range_result.structured_content["changed"] is True
    assert _read_raw_nb(edit_nb).cells[0].source == 'payload = "range"'

    insert_result = await mcp.call_tool("edit_notebook", {"path": str(edit_nb), "edits": [dict(op="insert_cells", anchor_id=cell_id, cells=[dict(cell_type="code", source_lines=["inserted = True"])])]})
    assert insert_result.structured_content["changed"] is True
    inserted_id = _read_raw_nb(edit_nb).cells[1].id
    assert _read_raw_nb(edit_nb).cells[1].source == "inserted = True"

    move_result = await mcp.call_tool("edit_notebook", {"path": str(edit_nb), "edits": [dict(op="move_cells", cell_ids=[inserted_id], anchor_id=cell_id, where="before")]})
    assert move_result.structured_content["changed"] is True
    assert _read_raw_nb(edit_nb).cells[0].id == inserted_id

    delete_result = await mcp.call_tool("edit_notebook", {"path": str(edit_nb), "edits": [dict(op="delete_cells", cell_ids=[inserted_id])]})
    assert delete_result.structured_content["changed"] is True
```

### MCP log problem visibility

Short terminal reports still need to account for the whole log.
[`mcp_log_report`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/mcp.html#mcp_log_report)
keeps full problem counts and grouped classifications even when
`problems` is limited, so a compact report cannot hide systemic
failures.

``` python
debug = mcp_tool_result("context", {"target": "nbs/example.ipynb"}, long_output, detail="debug")
assert debug.structured_content["debug"]["arguments"] == {"target": "nbs/example.ipynb"}
assert debug.structured_content["debug"]["raw_output"] == long_output
assert "Result:" in debug.content[0].text

shape_cases = [
    (
        "context",
        {"target": "foo", "scope": "nbs"},
        "full context",
        {"context": {"resolved_kind": "symbol", "path": "nbs/a.ipynb", "symbol": "foo", "cells": [dict(path="nbs/a.ipynb", cell_id="abc123", source="def foo(): pass")]}},
        ("context completed", "resolved=symbol", "path=nbs/a.ipynb", "symbol=foo", "cells=1", "id=abc123"),
    ),
    (
        "context",
        {"target": "nbs", "include_re": "foo", "view": "full"},
        "full matches",
        {"context": {"resolved_kind": "filter", "selection": {"kind": "context_filter", "matches": [dict(path="nbs/a.ipynb", cell_id="abc123", cell_idx=7, source="#| export\ndef foo(): pass\nclass Bar:\n    def baz(self): pass")], "total_matches": 3}}},
        ("context completed", "resolved=filter", "matches=1 shown of 3", "id=abc123", "def foo(): pass", "class Bar:", "def baz(self): pass"),
    ),
    (
        "diff_nb",
        {"path": "nbs/a.ipynb"},
        "--- code cell abc123 ---\n-old\n+new\n",
        {},
        ("diff_nb completed", "changed_cells=1", "added_lines=1", "deleted_lines=1", "cells=abc123"),
    ),
    (
        "doctor",
        {"path": "nbs/a.ipynb"},
        "long doctor output",
        {"doctor": {"error_count": 1, "warning_count": 1}},
        ("doctor completed", "errors=1 warnings=1"),
    ),
    (
        "reference",
        {"action": "query", "query": "foo"},
        "{}",
        {"reference": {"backend": "local", "hits": [dict(module="pkg.mod", symbol="thing", dependency_status="direct", score=0.91)]}},
        ("reference completed", "hits=1 backend=local", "pkg.mod.thing: direct score=0.91"),
    ),
    (
        "edit_notebook",
        {"path": "nbs/a.ipynb", "dry_run": True},
        "full diff",
        {"edit_notebook": {"changed": True, "dry_run": True, "affected_cell_ids": ["abc123"], "diffs": [dict(changed=True)]}},
        ("edit_notebook completed", "changed=True", "dry_run=True", "affected_cells=1", "cells=abc123"),
    ),
]

old_doctor_warnings = globals().get("_doctor_warnings")
try:
    globals()["_doctor_warnings"] = lambda *args, **kwargs: []
    for tool, arguments, raw, structured, fragments in shape_cases:
        result = mcp_tool_result(tool, arguments, raw, **structured)
        summary = result.content[0].text
        assert "Result:" not in summary
        assert not {"summary", "full_output", "preview_output"} & result.structured_content.keys()
        for fragment in fragments:
            assert fragment in summary, (tool, fragment, summary)
finally:
    globals()["_doctor_warnings"] = old_doctor_warnings
```

``` python
def _capture_mcp_warning_scopes():
    try:
        def fake_doctor_warnings(path=".", scope_path=None, scope_cell_ids=None):
            cell_scope = None if scope_cell_ids is None else set(scope_cell_ids)
            calls.append((path, scope_path, cell_scope))
            return []

        globals()["_doctor_warnings"] = fake_doctor_warnings
        mcp_tool_result("healthcheck", {}, "ok")
        mcp_tool_result("context", {"target": "nbs"}, "Project context")
        mcp_tool_result("context", {"target": "nbs/chapter.ipynb"}, "Cell id=ch1\nCell id=ch2")
        mcp_tool_result("diff_nb", {"path": "nbs/07_mcp.ipynb"}, "diff without cell ids")
        mcp_tool_result("diff_nb", {"path": "nbs/07_mcp.ipynb"}, "--- code cell abc123 ---\nchanged")
        mcp_tool_result("edit_notebook", {"path": "nbs/update_scope.ipynb", "edits": [dict(op="replace_cell", cell_id="upd123", source_lines=["x"])]}, "edit_notebook changed")
        mcp_tool_result("edit_notebook", {"path": "nbs/batch_a.ipynb", "edits": [dict(op="replace_cell", path="nbs/batch_b.ipynb", cell_id="b1", source_lines=["b"])]}, "edit_notebook changed")
    finally:
        globals()["_doctor_warnings"] = old_doctor_warnings
```

``` python
original_stdout = sys.stdout
outputs = []
errors = []
entered = threading.Event()
```

``` python
def _slow_print(label, delay, signal=None):
    def inner():
        if signal is not None: signal.set()
        time.sleep(delay)
        print(label)
    return inner
```

``` python
def _capture_worker(label, delay, signal=None):
    try:
        outputs.append(capture_call(_slow_print(label, delay, signal=signal)))
    except BaseException as exc:
        errors.append(exc)
```

``` python
cell_stdout = sys.stdout
threads = [
    threading.Thread(target=_capture_worker, args=("first", 0.03, entered)),
    threading.Thread(target=_capture_worker, args=("second", 0.01)),
]
threads[0].start()
assert entered.wait(1)
threads[1].start()
for thread in threads: thread.join()

assert errors == []
assert sorted(outputs) == ["first", "second"]
assert sys.stdout is cell_stdout
```
